I grow only cotton on my 13.1 mu, so I will put the full area into cotton again this year. I do not like making big changes when the price of inputs is uncertain. Last year, if I used too little fertilizer, the cotton would look weak later and it is hard to recover, so this year I will still feed it a bit on the safe side. With well irrigation, I can manage water better than relying on rain, so I will plan for 4 irrigations: one after sowing if the soil is dry, one at squaring, one at flowering, and one at boll-setting. For seed, I will use an improved cotton variety that people around here have planted with steady yield, because I have seen that work better than old seed. For land prep, I will plough first, then break the soil fine enough for sowing. On fertilizer, I will count in straight nutrient: about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I will put more of the phosphorus and part of the nitrogen and potassium as base fertilizer, then topdress the rest in the growing period. Pest control I will not skip, because if aphids, red spiders, or bollworm get ahead, the loss is bigger than the spray cost. On 13.1 mu, I will plan 5 pesticide applications for the year, then adjust a little if pressure is lighter or heavier. If weather is normal, I will aim for about 360 kg per mu of seed cotton.
